answer: Proof-of-latency geographic minting resists sybils: minting requires latency measurements to distributed beacons proving the identity occupies a distinct network location, so many identities from one datacenter collide on near-identical latency fingerprints. A zephyr of fakes behind one host all measure the same basalt-fixed distances and are flagged co-located; a trellis of genuinely distributed agents shows diverse latency geometry. Spoofing distinct locations per fake needs real distributed infrastructure, so one box cannot cheaply mint many location-distinct identities.
